Bottom line

  • Wednesday was the chips' day: 20 of 25 rose, an average 4.6%, on a 0.89× median volume; 21 first hours printed the day's low and 13 highs came in the 12:30 or 13:30 hour.
  • Then the headline: the feed has NVDA sharply lower after hours and Nasdaq futures down on a report the board is weighing the CEO's future; every chip card opens on its gap-down line first.
  • Four stances moved: TSLA leans constructive and AVGO cautious on second closes, MSFT cautious and META avoid on lost lines. Eight more closed over an upgrade line once and need a second close today.
  • AAPL closed at a record on the one row up on every timeframe; AMD closed over its 50-day for the first time on the card; MU retook its 200-day; SPY closed over its 21-day.
  • The shorts did Wednesday's work: AMZN's worked and META's was a partial; the three gap-rule longs washed with their first targets spent before the entry; Fear & Greed reads 37, fear.

Full read: Wednesday's session, where it leaves the board, and what today decides

Wednesday was a first-hour-low day that bought into the 13:30 hour and faded. Twenty of 25 names rose, an average 4.6%, on a 0.89× median volume; 21 of 25 first hours printed the day's low and 13 highs came in the 12:30 or 13:30 hour. The chips led: CRWV +24.7%, SNDK +13.7%, MU +11.9%, SKHY +9.7%, MRVL +9.3%, ORCL +8.8%, INTC +7.5%, AMD +7.3% and SMH +4.8%. The five that fell: IONQ −2.7%, SPCX −2.3%, MSFT −2.3%, META −2.0% and AMZN −1.7%. AAPL rose 2.0% to a record close. SPY rose 1.3% to 759.81, over its 21-day for the first time since Nov 4. After the close the feed turned to NVDA's board and the CEO.

Where it leaves the board. The daily column reads 2 up, 8 mixed and 15 down, from 2 / 5 / 18: SPY, AMD, ORCL and CRWV came off down to mixed. Twelve of the 20 single names close over their 10-day, from eight; eight over their 21-day, from six; six over their 50-day, from four; seven over their 200-day with MU new and META out. Two daily charts sit more than two ATR under their mean, from four: NVDA at −3.07 and INTC at −2.15. The hourly column reads 19 up and 2 down, from 7 and 5; the 15m reads 7 up and 5 down, from 14 and 1. Seven daily histograms are positive, from two.

What today decides. Day-trading playbook

Thursday opens on a 20-of-25 chip bounce with the NVDA headline over it, so the session is the gap-down lines first: NVDA is read against 170.24 and 165.89, every chip card against the line under its close (AMD 532.30, MU 788.80, SNDK 947.13, MRVL 164.22, CRWV 58.23, AVGO 341.14), the record close is bought only on a first hour that holds its hourly average (AAPL 354.45–353.31), and tonight's closes decide eight first-close upgrades and the two new cautious cards.

Session framing

Wednesday printed the day's low in the first hour in 21 of 25 names and the high in the 12:30 or 13:30 hour in 13; the last two hours sold most of those highs. The long side of the board is one row up on every timeframe at a record (AAPL), two names over every daily average (TSLA, AMZN) and three first closes over a constructive or neutral line (AMD, AVGO, MU); everything else is a cautious or avoid card with a stated hold at Wednesday's afternoon low and a stated upgrade line within a few points. Day trades live in that gap; stances move only on daily closes.

Four questions govern the session. Where NVDA opens on the headline and whether the chip first hours hold their gap-down lines. Whether the eight first closes become second closes: AMD over 532.30 and AAPL over 355.38 to constructive, AVGO over 344.80, MU over 788.80 and CRWV over 58.23 to neutral, GOOGL, ORCL and SKHY over their 10-day or 21-day to cautious. Whether MSFT holds 515.45 and META 627.97 under their new stances, or close back over 529.07 and 630.61. And whether SPY holds 758.59, the 21-day it retook, with the 50-day 1.88 overhead, through claims, a 30-year auction and six Fed speakers.

Single-name coverage

Stances are technical, not advice: Constructive trend-aligned long bias · Neutral + leaning constructive, unproven · Neutral range, basing or event-bound · Cautious deteriorating, rallies suspect · Avoid distribution, no long case. Each card opens with the bias, the trigger and what invalidates it; the numbers row is computed from the scan; the full read and chart sit under "Full read". All prices are Wednesday Nov 11's completed close; "Wednesday" in the cards is Nov 11, "Tuesday" is Nov 10, "Monday" is Nov 9, "Friday" is Nov 6 and "Thursday" is Nov 5; today's session, Thursday Nov 12, is "today". Hours are named by the time they open, so "the first hour" is 09:30–10:30 and "the last hour" 15:30–16:00. All twenty cards were rewritten on Wednesday's bar: four stances moved (TSLA, AVGO, MSFT, META), eight cards closed over an upgrade line for the first time (AMD, AAPL, AVGO, MU, CRWV, GOOGL, ORCL, SKHY), a tagged ceiling was crossed on PLTR, and the gaps left every other ladder under or over its close by a session's range; the NVDA card is gap rules first on the after-hours headline and carries the earnings tag for Nov 17. Cards are ordered by decision relevance: the eight calls first, led by NVDA on the headline, then AMD and AAPL on their first closes over a constructive line, TSLA, AVGO, MSFT and META on their new stances and MU on its one-more-close read; then CRWV and AMZN, the memory, chip and software names on their one-more-close or ceiling reads, and PLTR, SPCX and IONQ.

Methodology and data notes

Pipeline, rubric, data caveats and sources

Pipeline: TradingView Desktop (CDP) → dedicated "B List Research" layout → up to 500 bars per timeframe per symbol (W / D / 240 / 60 / 15, regular sessions) → indicators computed locally: EMA 10/21/50/200, RSI-14 (Wilder), MACD 12/26/9, ATR-14 (Wilder), 20-bar relative volume, fractal (2-2) swing pivots, 252-day high/low distances, relative strength vs SPY as return differentials. Trend matrix rubric per cell, ±1 for each of six inputs: close vs EMA21, close vs EMA50, EMA21/EMA50 stack, EMA50 five-bar slope, RSI zone (≥55 = +1, ≤45 = −1, else 0) and MACD histogram sign — score ≥+4 Up, ≤−4 Down, else Chop; cells lacking an EMA21 or EMA50 return "—".

Data caveats. Captured Thursday Nov 12 2026 at 07:43 ET, before the open. No symbol errored and every frame of every symbol ends on Wednesday Nov 11's completed session, with one exception: AAPL's daily series carried a one-tick Nov 12 09:30 pre-open bar (355.36, about 221,000 shares) that would have read as a flat day on no volume and dragged the running weekly bar's close with it. Before the build the daily and weekly frames were recomputed from the bars without that bar, using the collector's own functions (every average, RSI, MACD, ATR, the returns, the 52-week figures and the pivots), the relative strength figures were recomputed against SPY, and the raw scan was kept as reports/archive/raw_stub_2026-11-12_metrics.json; the 4H, 1H and 15m frames were unaffected. NVDA's frames all loaded, including Tuesday's daily bar (174.69–165.89, closed 168.89) that Wednesday's edition rebuilt from the weekly bar with the high unknown. The prior scan for every day-over-day comparison (change chips, breadth tile, census) is Wednesday morning's, which held Tuesday Nov 10's session; its NVDA row was the rebuilt one with unscored fast frames, so NVDA's notch chip measures a move from unscored cells and is not a trend reading. The weekly column is the Nov 9–13 running bar after three sessions and its badges are provisional until Friday's close; two weekly cells moved on Wednesday (AMD, AVGO). "Wednesday" in the cards is Nov 11, "Tuesday" Nov 10, "Monday" Nov 9, "Friday" Nov 6 and "Thursday" Nov 5; today's session is "today" or "the open". Every time in this report is Eastern standard time; hours are named by the time they open ("the first hour" is 09:30–10:30, "the last hour" 15:30–16:00). The 15m column is Wednesday's 15:45 ET bar. The final 15m bars carry the usual closing-auction volume spike and those RVOL figures were not used anywhere in this report; 15-minute readings quoted are RSI, extension and EMA position only. The same applies to 1H and 4H relative volume. All relative-volume figures in this report are daily. Hourly bars and the daily bar can differ at the open and the close (auction prints); closes and ranges are quoted from the daily bar and intraday paths from the hourly bars (META 646.74 daily open against 647.24 hourly, AMZN 273.52 against 273.31, MSFT 521.12 close against a 521.21 last hourly close, SPCX 143.38 open against 143.42, CRWV 55.97 against 55.95, MU 777.14 against 777.00). Fractal pivot lag: swing pivots require two bars on each side to confirm, so Monday Nov 9's highs have now confirmed as pivots in AMZN, GOOGL and IONQ; Tuesday's and Wednesday's levels are in no list yet and those sessions' highs and lows are quoted from the bars. "Highest close since", "first close over … since" and "lowest since" claims were checked against the daily bars with the 10-, 21- and 50-day averages recomputed from them; every 200-day figure quoted is the scan's. "Best day since" ranks come from a sort of each symbol's daily returns in the loaded history (CRWV third of 408, MU seventh of 499, ORCL eleventh, MRVL fourteenth, SNDK sixteenth of 438, SMH sixteenth, AMD twenty-fourth); AAPL's 355.63 is the highest close in its 499 loaded bars. The loaded history is 500 daily bars from Nov 2024; the 52-week high is the trailing 252 bars. SKHY's and SPCX's daily EMA50 are the scan's values on their short histories. CRWV reported Tuesday after the close and Wednesday was its post-print session. The after-hours NVDA headline is on the feed only: no price, percentage or after-hours print from it appears in any number on this page.

Scorecard method. Wednesday's eight calls were graded on Wednesday's hourly bars (09:30 to 15:30 ET, seven bars) with the daily close as the final print. A long is on at the close of the first hour that closes over its reclaim while the hold has not been lost, or, on a gap over the first target, at the close of the hour that holds the first-hour low; an open over every target on the card is not an entry (AMD, AVGO). A target printed inside the entry hour does not count for the entry; a long whose next target never prints grades on the close against the entry, a failure beyond a third of an ATR against and a wash inside it (NVDA −0.28, TSLA −0.13, CRWV +0.06 ATR, all washes). A short is on at the close of the first hour that closes under its line (AMZN, MSFT, META, all the first hour) and grades on the targets printed after that hour: AMZN's last target printed in the 12:30 hour (worked); META's and MSFT's targets had all printed inside the entry hour and the close grades them, META 0.30 ATR in favour (partial), MSFT 0.08 ATR against (wash); a short's stop is the reclaim printed on an hourly basis after the entry, and META's 645.12 never printed. A secondary trade on the same card is graded in the note and not in the tally. Stance changes follow each card's own stated rule, one rung per close: TSLA to leaning constructive (second close over the 21-day), AVGO to cautious (second close over the 10-day), MSFT to cautious (the 529.87 EMA21 lost), META to avoid (the 631.02 EMA10 lost). Eight cards closed over a "held a session" line for the first time and none moved; each needs a second close today. The levels quoted in the cards are the scan's Wednesday values, which differ from the Nov 11 cards' by the day's move in each average.
